title: Anatomy of a Paradigm Shift: How the Transformer Architecture Redefined Natural Language Processing
hook: Opening with the computational bottlenecks of recurrent models, this post examines how replacing recurrence with pure self-attention eliminated sequential dependency and unlocked modern LLM scaling laws.

sections.heading: The Bottleneck of Sequential Computation in Recurrent Networks
key_points: Analyzing hidden state dependencies in LSTMs and GRUs that prevent parallelization during training
The degradation of gradient signals over long sequences due to vanishing and exploding gradient paths
The $O(N)$ computational complexity per layer that creates prohibitive wall-clock training times on massive corpora

sections.heading: Mathematical Formulation of Scaled Dot-Product and Multi-Head Attention
key_points: Deconstructing the Query, Key, and Value projections as differentiable information retrieval mechanisms
The scaling factor $\frac{1}{\sqrt{d_k}}$ preventing softmax saturation in high-dimensional spaces
Partitioning embedding subspaces into multiple heads to capture diverse syntactic and semantic relationships simultaneously

sections.heading: Eliminating Recurrence with Positional Encodings and Layer Normalization
key_points: Injecting token sequence order via sinusoidal functions and learned absolute/relative positional embeddings
Comparing Pre-LN versus Post-LN architectural placements for training stability in deep networks
Achieving $O(1)$ path length between any two tokens to mitigate the long-range dependency problem

sections.heading: Unlocking Scaling Laws and Foundation Models
key_points: How hardware-efficient matrix multiplications on GPUs enabled unprecedented parameter scaling
The transition from task-specific architectures to universal pre-training and downstream fine-tuning paradigms
Paving the road for emergent behaviors in models with hundreds of billions of parameters

conclusion_point: The Transformer's substitution of recurrence with parallelizable self-attention fundamentally altered NLP by turning sequence modeling into a high-throughput matrix multiplication problem, enabling the modern era of foundation models.
topic: Why the Transformer architecture changed NLP
